source_argument: Both items named by the scenario are TARGET-SIDE DEBUFFS, not attacker-local buffs. Black Cleaver's Carve is an armor REDUCTION on the enemy champion, and Bloodsong's Expose Weakness makes the debuffed champion 'take 8%/5% increased damage FROM ALL SOURCES'. In a coupled roster both therefore amplify every roster member's damage on that target, not just the holder's pair fight. Correct merging can only push the debuffed target's health path DOWN relative to a pair-local (un-merged) model — i.e. more missing health at any later timestamp, hence STRICTLY LESS overheal on a heal landing on that target. The direction of the change (37.4 -> 22.2) is the direction correct merging predicts; the larger old value is the un-merged/pair-local direction.

Neither cached effect amplifies HEALING. Bloodsong's Expose Weakness is stated in the cache as increased DAMAGE taken; Black Cleaver's Carve is armor reduction. Nothing in data/items.json, data/runes.json or docs/math-foundations.md sources a rule by which a damage amplifier scales a heal. The one exactly-round algebraic fit of the observed pair — heal 190.0 (new) vs 205.2 (old) = 190.0 x 1.08, i.e. exactly Bloodsong's melee Expose Weakness factor applied to the heal itself, with the recipient missing 167.8 health — is an UNSOURCED amplification in the old baseline and its removal is the sourced behavior.

The remaining feasible family (a melee/ranged variant correction, e.g. Conqueror's heal 8% melee / 5% ranged, factor 0.625) also points to the new, smaller value: the cached attack type is the source of truth for a champion's basic-attack class in its default form (e.g. data/champions.json Gnar -> "attackType": "RANGED"; the melee variant belongs only to an explicitly-toggled transformed form), so the ranged (smaller) variant is the sourced default and the melee (larger) variant is the unsourced one.
Consistency floor: overheal <= heal amount. Both values satisfy it, so it does not discriminate; the discriminator is the debuff-sharing / amplifier-scope direction above.
independent_computation.conclusion: Every mechanism in this scenario that the cached sources actually license moves this leaf DOWN from the un-merged baseline (shared target-side debuffs lower the target's health path; damage amplifiers do not scale heals; the sourced default melee/ranged variant is the smaller one). 22.2 is on the correct side of all of them; 37.4 is only reachable by amplifying a heal with a damage amplifier or by leaving a target-side debuff pair-local, neither of which is sourced.

**Black Cleaver average stacks** (`ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction`): the established model uses a fixed `0.8*max_stacks` constant (with a `hits/2` short-fight branch) ... the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes. — bounds how much of a 68% swing Black Cleaver's own approximation could possibly explain: it cannot (its damage effect is bounded by (100+A)/(100+0.7A) < 1.4286 for any armor A, versus the 1.685 ratio implied by 37.4/22.2).

The `_later_target_amount` receipt design is correct: each pair fight cannot see the roster, so the engine authors the full value with an explicit reduced receipt; the coupled ledger re-prices defenders past the first (`defender_index > 0`). — confirms that in this engine the coupled/roster ledger is the layer that re-prices values a pair fight over-authored, i.e. coupled re-pricing legitimately moves roster leaves DOWN.
